title: Chapter Nine
html:
Haridasa in Phuliya. The deliverance of a prostitute. Haridasa before the Muslim governor. The deliverance of a serpent. Haridasa and the brahmanas of Shantipura

1. Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees! 2. One day Thakura Sri Brahma Haridasa humbly told the Lord the desire of his heart: 3. "O Lord, allow me to go into solitude, so that I may ceaselessly taste the nectar of the name of Hari." 4. The Lord replied: "Separation from you breaks My heart, but I cannot forbid it — that would hinder your bhajana." 5. Haridasa prostrated himself at the Lord's feet, and the Lord in the ecstasy of love embraced him tightly. 6. Haridasa said: "I am an untouchable sinner. Why do You make me an offender by touching my body?" 7. The Lord replied: "I do not understand what high or low caste is: whoever worships Krishna is of the caste of Vaishnavas. 8. A person is called high or low according to his deeds: whoever worships Krishna I call the best of all. 9. You are the best among pure bhagavatas: by your touch the seed of devotion sprouts in a soul." 10. Haridasa said: "Lord, everything is possible if Your most pure mercy falls upon a soul." 11. Having said this, he joined his palms, received the Lord's leave and, remembering Hari, set out for the village of Phuliya. 12. All the brahmanas living in that town were moved at heart on seeing Haridasa. 13. There was a learned brahmana there named Ramadasa — versed in the scriptures of dharma, ever devoted to dharma. 14. Seeing Haridasa, he was filled with devotion and spoke humbly and kindly: 15. "Sadhu, by your coming we are made fortunate. I do not know how much merit our village had from the past! 16. By association with a sadhu a house becomes holy. Have mercy, master, and settle here." 17. Brahma Haridasa said: "O best of brahmanas, according to the Vedas every brahmana is the body of Vishnu. 18. I am of low birth and not fit to be touched. That I have obtained your company is my great good fortune." 19. Ramadasa said: "Sadhu, why such humility? For one who loves God, caste is not counted. 20. As iron becomes gold at the touch of the philosopher's stone, so in the worship of God every class becomes the best. 21. What is there to praise in a person? One should praise his dharma: high or low one is called by one's own deeds. 22. Whoever has given up worldly desires and loves God is the best of all beings and has a share in liberation." 23. Haridasa replied: "You are a sadhu by nature: you see sadhus in all beings. 24. Whoever worships God by the path of knowledge attains only liberation — according to the power of his knowledge. 25. The wise sadhu does not desire liberation: by the path of knowledge alone a soul does not obtain eternal freedom." 26. The brahmana asked: "What is there besides knowledge through which the Supreme Brahman, the essence of essences, is attained?" 27. Brahma Haridasa replied: "The essence of all is the path of devotion: by it the eternal Brahman, the Lord of all, is attained. 28. By the nature of devotion the self-conception of a servant arises, and to His servant Hari gives an eternally perfect body. 29. The eternal reality of Brahman is Bhagavan Himself, full of being, consciousness and bliss, all-powerful. 30. The name of Hari is the cause of pure devotion: whoever chants it ceaselessly obtains the eternal treasure of love. 31. When love gradually deepens, one attains the mood of the gopis, and in the sweet rasa of madhurya one attains Radha and Krishna." 32. Hearing this, the brahmana's hair stood on end all over his body, and he said: "Have mercy, initiate me." 33. Hearing this, Haridasa, full of love, imparted power to the brahmana and gave him the name of Hari. 34. Having obtained the greatest treasure, the brahmana shed floods of tears; he bowed to Haridasa and offered him praise. 35. Gradually, in the company of the sadhu, the brahmana became a Vaishnava, and in the field of his heart the wish-fulfilling creeper of devotion sprang up. 36. With the brahmana's help Brahma Haridasa built a hut and lived in it joyfully. 37. He ceaselessly tasted the nectar of the name of Hari, and all the villagers became his devotees. 38. One day Haridasa reflected: "It is not good to live long in one place. 39. From conversation and company comes a connection with maya, and little by little the soul is blinded by attachment to the world. 40. Thus the dharma of the detached is not preserved; therefore it is best to give up the company of people." 41. Thinking thus, at the end of the night he left his dwelling and, singing the name of Hari, went to Benapol. 42. There, in the midst of a dense forest, he sang sankirtana, and the people of the village came to worship him. 43. That greatly fortunate one to whom Krishna is merciful — every being who sees him is filled with devotion. 44. Seeing the radiance emanating from the body of Brahma Haridasa, gradually all the villagers became his devotees. 45. In that forest of Benapol the village devotees carefully built him a hut. 46. Living there, the sadhu served Tulasi and chanted ten million Names in a month. 47. He begged a handful of rice as alms in the houses of Vaishnava brahmanas; such is the nature of mercy: to teach the souls righteousness. 48. One day a prostitute, like a Vidyadhari in beauty, dressed herself up and came to Haridasa. 49. Sitting at the door of the hut, she began to display her body. Haridasa asked her kindly: 50. "Why have you come here in the evening?" The prostitute replied: "Seeing you, I have lost my head. 51. You have wondrous beauty and fresh youth: give up your sankirtana and enjoy pleasures." 52. Hearing this, Haridasa replied with a smile: "Go away from here today. 53. Whoever does not wear tulasi beads on the neck, whoever does not apply tilaka to the forehead, 54. on whose lips the name of Krishna does not appear — such people are contemptible unbelievers. 55. Know for certain: they have turned away from Krishna, and a sadhu never looks at their faces. 56. If you come in such a holy guise, then Krishna will fulfil your desire." 57. Having said this, the sadhu went on with his sankirtana, and the prostitute went home. 58. The next day she put tulasi beads round her neck and applied tilaka of gopichandana clay to her forehead. 59. Writing the names of Hari on her body, she dressed as a Vaishnavi and in the evening came to Haridasa. 60. Bowing to Vrinda (Tulasi), she sat at the door of the hut and for show loudly repeated: "Hari, Hari." 61. Boundless is the unearthly power of the company of saints: even by assuming a holy guise in pretence a soul obtains liberation in this life. 62. As an ordinary tree, standing beside sandalwood, absorbs its fragrance and itself becomes sandalwood. 63. Hearing the ceaseless name of Hari from the prostitute's lips, the crown of Vaishnavas praised her in the bliss of love. 64. Hearing the praise, the prostitute said to Haridasa: "Master, have mercy on me — for this I have come." 65. Hearing this, Haridasa said: "It is good that you have come. Say just once in a full voice: 'Hari, Hari.'" 66. Having said this, he began to sing the sankirtana of the Name, and listening to his singing the prostitute's heart was changed. 67. Through the shock of holy company she came to her senses and understood that the trade of a prostitute is nothing but the enjoyment of sin. 68. Bowing to Haridasa, she said with joined palms: "You are a great magnet-jewel: you have drawn me. 69. You are my master, my guru, a merciful wish-fulfilling tree. Take my side and grant me the fruit of liberation." 70. Hearing the prostitute's words, full of longing for dharma and firm faith, the crown of sadhus was immersed in the sweetness of love. 71. As atonement he shaved her head and, imparting power, gave the name of Hari into her ears. 72. Having received the name of Hari, she put forth a sprout of love, and Haridasa named her Krishnadasi. 73. The sadhu said: "Live here and chant the name of Hari: by the power of Krishna's mercy the desire of your heart will be fulfilled. 74. Brahman as the Name has the same power as the Supreme Brahman: through the Name one attains Krishna, and through a semblance of the Name — liberation." 75. Having said this, Haridasa went to another place, and Krishnadasi chanted the name of Krishna day and night. 76. Astonishing is the inconceivable power of a sadhu's mercy: a poisonous tree bears fruits of unearthly nectar. 77. Now hear of a wondrous pastime of Haridasa: how he made many yavanas servants of Krishna. 78. All the Vaishnavas living in the village of Phuliya were immersed in bliss on seeing Haridasa. 79. Gathering together, they ceaselessly sang the sankirtana of the Name, and it was as if a spear pierced the hearts of the unbelievers. 80. The governor of the yavanas, learning about Haridasa, in great anger said to his servants: 81. "In Phuliya there is a man named Haridasa: himself a yavana, he does the things of Hindus. 82. People laugh at him, and little by little the faith of the yavanas will perish. 83. Therefore seize him, bring him here and punish him." Receiving the command, the wicked servants ran off. 84. Seizing Haridasa and treating him with violence, they brought him to court with his hands bound. 85. Seeing Haridasa, the governor of the yavanas said: "Why do you, being of high caste, behave like a Hindu? 86. Whoever abandons his own religion and devotes himself to a great work (of another faith) will surely go to hell after death. 87. If you have in your mind the desire to reach paradise, recite the kalima and atone for your sin." 88. Hearing this, Haridasa replied in a deep voice: "I call that scripture best which is founded on reason. 89. Whoever follows a scripture consistent with reason is the best in all classes — so say the shastras. 90. The scripture of the yavanas contradicts reason: whoever follows it shows himself a yavana. 91. Here is the proof: the cow is mother and father, and an argument for killing the cow contradicts reason. 92. To eat its flesh is the same as eating one's father's flesh; yet their scripture prescribes killing the cow. 93. The births of these impious people multiply: by the fruits of their deeds they wander through various species of life. 94. The Supreme Brahman is the very being of all, the beginningless form (vigraha), full of the six opulences, with a body of pure goodness. 95. Scriptures that call Him formless and inactive — by reading them the delusion of maya grows. 96. In essence there is no difference between God and the soul — as the nature of fire is one in all lamps, 97. and yet the original fire remains chief; so Hari is the Lord of all and the support of all. 98. If one worships Hari, the soul's maya vanishes; with this aspiration I have taken shelter at the feet of Hari." 99. Hearing from the sadhu's lips proofs consistent with reason, all considered him a pir (a saint). 100. At that time the sadhu displayed his power, and the mlecchas, seeing it, were terrified. 101. Taking a straw between his teeth, the governor of the yavanas said: "O sadhu, be merciful to me, a lowly one. 102. I am ignorant and wicked: not recognizing you, I have committed an offence. Forgive me. 103. To your feet my millions of obeisances. By your goodness deliver me now, insignificant as I am." 104. Hearing this, Haridasa was moved to mercy and blessed him: "May your mind turn to Krishna." 105. Raising his arms, he said: "Say 'Hari, Hari': breaking the bonds of karma, you will obtain the boat of devotion." 106. Hearing this, all were filled with devotion and, crying "Hari, Hari," broke into dance. 107. Thus Haridasa delivered the yavanas and from there came to the town of Kuliya. 108. Boundless is the glory of Brahma Haridasa: even the gods do not know it — what then of insignificant me? 109. Through association with him Gosani Raghunatha Dasa obtained the seed of devotion and faith in Chaitanya. 110. He by whose mercy a serpent attained liberation in this life — what wonder if he delivered the yavanas? 111. Now I shall briefly tell of the deliverance of the serpent: hearing it, one comes to know the glory of a Vaishnava. 112. Haridasa sat in a cave chanting the name of Hari; hearing it, all the villagers came to him. 113. Seeing the sadhu's love and his taste for the Name, all began to sing the sankirtana of the Name with him every day. 114. At that time an enormous black serpent appeared: on its head a divine jewel blazed like the sun. 115. It stopped before Haridasa, coiled itself up and listened to the name of Hari. 116. Seeing this, all trembled with fear and said: "Best of sadhus, today you will lose your life." 117. Then the sadhu fearlessly took the serpent by the neck and, imparting his power to it, gave it the name of Hari. 118. Clapping his hands, he sang the name of Hari, and the serpent, hearing it, danced round in love. 119. Tears flowed ceaselessly from both its eyes; again and again it bowed its head to the Vaishnava's feet. 120. Receiving the dust of the Vaishnava's feet and hearing Brahman as the name of Hari, 121. the serpent before their eyes obtained a perfect body and, becoming four-armed, departed for the divine Vrindavana. 122. All the people, seeing this inconceivable glory, became Vaishnavas and devoted themselves to the name of Hari. 123. After some days a longing seized the sadhu, and he appeared in holy Shantipura. 124. Sri Advaita Prabhu, seeing His beloved Haridasa, said, "Come, father!" and floated on the waves of the bliss of love. 125. Seeing Shripada Prabhu, Brahma Haridasa prostrated himself with the eight limbs of his body and spoke humbly. 126. The Lord embraced him and said sweet words: "Give up your humility — I consider you equal to My own life." 127. In talk of the Beloved both were immersed in love and, crying "Hari!", raised their arms and broke into dance. 128. Thus day by day the festival grew. The high-caste brahmanas said among themselves: 129. "If the Acharya does not give up His association with Haridasa, He must certainly be excluded from the community." 130. The Acharya paid no attention to this, and the unbelievers excluded the Lord. 131. The Lord said: "Good, good — bad company is gone: Bhagavan has shown Me mercy." 132. Hear a wondrous account: in Shantipura there lived a rich high-caste brahmana. 133. Invited to an auspicious ceremony at his house, more than a hundred brahmanas came in great delight. 134. Having been honoured, all took their seats. At that time a certain sannyasi came there. 135. His form shone like the sun; by the radiance of his body all the directions were lit up. 136. He sat under a tree and did not utter a word; all the people came and bowed to him. 137. All the blind, the dumb and the others who came to the sadhu smeared their whole bodies with the dust of his lotus feet. 138. By the touch of the dust of the sadhu's feet their ailments went away, and all of them in great joy broke into dance. 139. The blind received sight, the lame received feet, the dumb spoke — their misfortunes passed. 140. Seeing this wonder, all the high-caste brahmanas, proud of their learning, and the unbelievers 141. came and bowed at the sadhu's feet, tying cloths round their necks, and offered him praises of many kinds. 142. For the sake of serving the sadhu they humbled themselves greatly. The sadhu said: "I eat nothing but the prasada of Vishnu. 143. The prasada of Vishnu is supremely holy; food not offered to Vishnu is like filth. 144. The gods, the ancestors and the saints accept nothing but what has been offered to Vishnu. 145. Whoever disregards this eternal word of the shruti will surely fall into a terrible hell." 146. The host of the ceremony said: "In my house there is Narayana; I shall offer you His prasada." 147. Saying "So be it," the sadhu agreed, and then they seated him in the assembly of brahmanas. 148. Like the moon amid the host of constellations, so the best of sadhus shone amid the assembly of brahmanas. 149. They carefully served the sadhu his food, and then began to serve it to the brahmanas. 150. When the feeding of the brahmanas was over, the Lord came there. 151. The all-knowing Sri Advaita, the guru of the world, is a wish-fulfilling tree for the pure devotees. 152. Seeing Brahma Haridasa in the assembly of brahmanas, the Lord smiled slightly and said gently: 153. "Dear Haridasa, what have you done? You have deprived so many brahmanas of their caste!" 154. Haridasa replied: "Lord, it was not my will: I sat down at the special insistence of the brahmanas." 155. Having said this, he quickly rinsed his mouth, bowed to the Lord and offered Him many praises. 156. Seeing this, the brahmanas were amazed and said: "The Acharya is Vishnu Himself come down to earth. 157. That Haridasa, for association with whom we excluded Him, is full of unearthly virtues. 158. The body of a devotee of Hari is perfectly pure: to see caste in him is a great sin. 159. We have offended the feet of Sri Advaita, and He out of mercy has taught us through His devotee." 160. Having said this, the brahmanas joined both palms, tied cloths round their necks and came to the Acharya. 161. Then the Lord out of mercy revealed His true form: Maha-Vishnu and Sadashiva — two in one form. 162. Seeing that form, the brahmanas were filled with ecstatic emotion: tears, trembling, the hair on their bodies standing up like kadamba flowers. 163. They said: "Lord, we take shelter at Your feet. Forgive our offence and place Your holy feet on our heads." 164. Prostrating themselves with the eight limbs of their bodies, they offered praise, and all drank the water that had washed the Lord's feet. 165. The Lord said: "Brahmanas, do not be afraid: the name of Hari has inconceivable great power. 166. Chant this Brahman as the Name and sing sankirtana — and the desires of all will be fulfilled without difficulty." 167. Having said this, Sri Advaita went home, and the brahmanas by great good fortune became Vaishnavas. 168. Boundless is the glory of the feet of a Sri Vaishnava: insignificant I do not know even a drop of it. 169. If, when good fortune dawns, a mleccha obtains devotion to Krishna, he obtains brahmanhood — so sing the Vedas. 170. As bronze becomes gold by a certain elixir, so by the path of devotion pure goodness is born. 171. The brahmanas had a base nature — by the power of a Vaishnava it was purified. 172. To reveal to the ignorant the glory of a Vaishnava, the Lord, passing over the brahmanas, gave the memorial dish (shraddha-patra) to Haridasa. 173. Haridasa, joining his palms, said to the Lord: "Why, instead of giving it to a brahmana, have You given the dish to me?" 174. The Lord replied: "A Sri Vaishnava has unearthly power: if you eat, it is the fruit of feeding ten million brahmanas." 175. Haridasa said: "You are the Sri Vaishnava-acharya: Your command must be accepted as scripture of dharma." 176. Hearing the name "Sri Vaishnava-acharya," the best of lords, overwhelmed with love, gave a loud roar. 177. In the company of Haridasa His jubilation grew; He constantly delighted in the kirtana of the name of Hari. 178. One day Haridasa said to the Lord: "The wicked mlecchas are destroying the eternal dharma. 179. They smash the Deities (murtis) of the gods to pieces and ruin everything needed for the worship of the gods. 180. The Srimad Bhagavatam and the other scriptures of dharma they seize by force and throw into the fire. 181. They take away the conches and bells of the brahmanas and forcibly lick off the tilaka and marks from their bodies. 182. They urinate on Sri Tulasi like dogs; in the temples they defecate like madmen. 183. Thus by hundreds of wicked deeds they contemptuously destroy every dharma and righteous act. 184. The firm vow of Krishna, known from the shastras: 'Whenever there is a decline of true dharma, 185. whenever adharma rises up — at every such time Krishna manifests Himself.' 186. Now that time has come. Why then has Krishnachandra not appeared? 187. How will dharma be protected, Lord? Thinking of this, I am constantly anxious." 188. The Lord replied: "Such is the way of this age of Kali: without the appearance of Krishna there is no remedy. 189. Bringing Krishna to appear, I shall spread the Name far and wide and deliver the whole world without difficulty." 190. Having said this, He roared loudly again and again, and Haridasa danced in the ecstasy of love. 191. Although Advaitachandra knows the whole truth, still He made a vow, following the custom of the world. 192. Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.

✦

Translator's notes

  • V. 87: kalima — the Muslim profession of faith.
  • Vv. 96–97: oneness of the soul and God in nature (like fire in many lamps) together with God's fullness and supremacy — in the spirit of the teaching of achintya-bhedabheda; this is not an assertion of their identity.
  • V. 99: pir — an honorific for a Muslim saint.
  • V. 172: shraddha-patra — the dish of the memorial meal, which by custom is given to the most worthy brahmana.
  • Vv. 184–185: a paraphrase of Bhagavad-gita 4.7.
